operations.specification: Registers a new user in the Todo List application by creating a pending user record in the todo_list_users table. Accepts a unique, valid email and a password meeting minimum security requirements. Upon registration, an email verification token and timestamp are generated and stored to support verification flows. Registration is restricted to unique, non-disposable emails and will fail with a clear explanation if violated. The user will not be able to log in or use the system until email verification is completed successfully.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables a new user to register for the Todo List application. The todo_list_users schema requires a unique email (field: email) and a securely hashed password (field: password_hash). Upon successful creation, a new user record is stored with is_verified set to false, email_verification_token generated, and email_verification_sent_at set.

The registration process enforces strict uniqueness on the email field and adheres to password policy (minimum length, includes letters and numbers). Immediate email verification is required—users cannot access other system features until the is_verified flag is true (see is_verified field in schema).

Registration details are stored in todo_list_users with lifecycle metadata, supporting further steps such as email verification.

Significant error cases include duplicate or invalid email (rejected via unique index and validation), and non-compliant password (explained to user).

After registration, the user should immediately receive an email verification request; no further actions are allowed until completed.
operations.summary: Register a new user in the todo_list_users table.

requestBody.description: User registration details: valid unique email and strong password.

responseBody.description: Authorized user after successful registration and verification.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticates an existing user against the todo_list_users table and creates a new session/audit record in todo_list_user_sessions. Validates provided credentials (email and password) and enforces account policies: must be verified (is_verified = true), not deleted (deleted_at is null), and not locked (locked = false). On success, issues JWT access/refresh tokens and logs session context (ip, href, referrer, created_at) in the sessions table. Handles audit policy and session invalidation on failed login, locked accounts, or non-verified email addresses.
operations.description:
This endpoint processes user login. Credentials are checked by matching the email (unique, field: email) and secure password (password_hash field, using secure verification operations). Login is blocked if the user's is_verified is false, the locked flag is true (with locked_at optionally set), or deleted_at is non-null.

Each successful login creates a record in todo_list_user_sessions, capturing session-related metadata (ip, href, referrer, created_at). All issued JWT tokens are scoped to the user and session, supporting later revocation.

Login attempts are audited; repeated failures toggle locked/locked_at according to business rules from requirements. If a user is locked out (locked = true), login is denied pending reset/unlock flow.

This endpoint does not reveal whether email or password was incorrect for security. All failed responses are generic.

Login is the sole means of initiating authenticated user sessions; all further API access requires a valid token from this flow.
operations.summary: Authenticate user for todo_list_users and create session record.

requestBody.description: User login credentials: email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorized user including fresh JWT tokens for session.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refreshes JWT access and refresh tokens for an authenticated user session. Consumes a valid refresh token—which must match an active session record in todo_list_user_sessions, not expired or revoked. Refresh endpoint will reject requests for locked, deleted, or non-verified users. On success, issues new tokens and logs the event in session audit logs per compliance requirements.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables a user to maintain a valid session by refreshing their JWT tokens. It verifies that the provided refresh token is active and corresponds to a valid, active session in todo_list_user_sessions.

Additional validation checks that the user's account is not locked (locked field), email is verified (is_verified field), and deleted_at is null. If any of these conditions fail, refresh is denied.

Upon success, new tokens are generated and session renewal is logged (session table fields: created_at, expired_at updated as needed).

Refresh tokens can only be used as long as the session is active and valid per expiration policy. Audit compliance is enforced for all refresh actions.

Token refresh is the sole mechanism for extending active user sessions without logging in again.
operations.summary: Refresh access/refresh tokens for authenticated user via session and todo_list_users.

responseBody.description: Authorized user including new tokens after refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Confirms a user's email address after registration by verifying the unique email_verification_token and updating the is_verified flag in the todo_list_users table. Allows activation of user account for subsequent login and feature access. Clears verification token on completion.
operations.description:
This endpoint is used to complete user registration by verifying the one-time token provided after signup. The token must exactly match the value stored in email_verification_token field on todo_list_users for the requesting user. Upon successful verification, is_verified is set to true and email_verification_token/email_verification_sent_at are cleared.

Successful verification unlocks the account for login and access to all self-managed features.

If the token is invalid, expired, or not found for the supplied email address, the operation fails gracefully with a generic error.

This flow is mandatory per requirements and is directly tied to account activation lifecycle.

Verification tokens are only valid for a set time after registration; after expiration, a new registration or resend process must be initiated.
operations.summary: Verify new user email (todo_list_users) to activate account.

requestBody.description: Email and verification token information for account activation.

responseBody.description: Outcome of verification and updated user status.

operations.name: verifyEmail

operations.specification: Initiates a password reset flow for a user in the todo_list_users table. Generates a new reset_password_token and reset_password_sent_at timestamp, and sends a secure expiring link to the user's registered email. Prevents information leakage—response is always generic regardless of email status. Does not permit operation if account is deleted or locked.
operations.description:
This endpoint initiates a secure password reset request. The email provided is checked against todo_list_users. If the user exists, a reset_password_token is generated, reset_password_sent_at is set, and the user is notified via email. If the user does not exist or is ineligible (deleted, locked), the response is identical for privacy/protection.

The reset token is valid for a fixed period (see requirements); after expiration, the process must be started again.

This operation does not return user existence or eligibility—in every case, the response is generic to avoid information leakage as mandated in requirements.

This operation is mandatory for account recovery and complies with sent_at and token storage in the schema.

Subsequent reset steps validate token and allow password update. All session tokens are revoked upon completion.
operations.summary: Request password reset for eligible user in todo_list_users.

requestBody.description: User email address for resetting password (no information leakage allowed).

operations.name: requestPasswordReset

operations.specification: Resets user's password by accepting the reset_password_token and new password, validating both, and updating the password_hash for the user in todo_list_users. Upon success, revokes all existing access/refresh tokens, marks reset_password_token as used (null), and ensures full session logout. Password strength and expiration checks are enforced.
operations.description:
This endpoint completes the password reset process by consuming a valid reset_password_token, a new password, and updating the user's password_hash. It checks token validity (matches and not expired), and on success, immediately wipes the reset_password_token and reset_password_sent_at fields and saves the new hash.

All current sessions and tokens are force-revoked for complete account protection (see audit requirements in sessions table).

Password requirements (min 8 chars, required letter and number) are strictly enforced as per requirements.

On error (e.g., invalid/expired token), response is generic to prevent information leakage.

Upon successful reset, user can only log in with new password and existing tokens are invalid.
operations.summary: Reset user password for todo_list_users with valid token and new password.

requestBody.description: Password reset submission: token and new password.

responseBody.description: Password reset result with underlying status.

operations.name: resetPassword

operations.specification: Unlocks a locked user account in the todo_list_users table after lockout caused by repeated failed logins or security events. Expects a valid unlock token or process as defined by business rules and updates locked/locked_at fields upon successful unlock. Supports audit and compliance needs as described.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows an eligible user to restore access to a locked account. It verifies that the locked field is set (locked = true, locked_at populated), and the provided unlock process or token matches business rules (may involve password reset, cooldown, or manual admin action).

Once verified, the locked flag is cleared, locked_at is set to null, and the account is eligible for login again.

All unlock operations are fully audited using fields in the user and session audit tables (locked, locked_at, and related session records).

Business rules for unlock are defined in requirements and commonly involve enforced cooldown or secure validation.

On success, user may immediately attempt login with their regular credentials.
operations.summary: Unlock locked user account in todo_list_users after lockout.

requestBody.description: Required data per unlock process (e.g., unlock token, validation steps).

responseBody.description: Outcome of unlock operation for account recovery.

operations.name: unlock

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of registered users for the Todo List application. It operates on the todo_list_users table as defined in the Prisma schema. The operation allows advanced searching with filter criteria such as username, email, registration date, and active status as supported by the schema. The results are paginated and can be sorted on key fields as required by business logic. The intended purpose is to allow authorized actors to locate users based on diverse search conditions, serving administrative search needs and potential user analytics.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of Todo List application users for administrative review or account management.

This operation provides advanced searching and sorting capabilities across all user entities. Administrators can filter by various criteria such as username, email, date ranges, and account status when approved by the schema's defined fields. Pagination helps in efficiently managing large user bases, with support for configurable page size and sorting by supported columns.

Security considerations include that only authorized actors can access this operation to protect personal data and limit search spam. The endpoint is tied to the todo_list_users table, confirming all properties and logic reference actual schema fields and business requirements. Related operations include retrieving single users and managing user access rights.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of registered Todo List users.

requestBody.description: Filter criteria, sorting, and pagination options for searching Todo List users.

responseBody.description: Paginated results listing user summary data that matches search criteria.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the detail data of a single registered user in the Todo List application, based on a unique user identifier. It references the todo_list_users table in the Prisma schema, fetching all available details for the specified userId. The intent is to allow authorized actors to review complete user information for support, auditing, or management purposes. The operation directly maps the userId path parameter to the underlying user entity.
operations.description:
Retrieve the complete details of a Todo List application user, identified by their unique userId.

This operation allows an administrator or authorized support staff to review all relevant data about a specific user, including personal details, registration metadata, and account status, as enabled by the schema fields. The path parameter userId corresponds directly to the unique identifier in the todo_list_users table. Access to this endpoint should be controlled to prevent unauthorized inspection of user data.

The endpoint returns a single ITodoListUser DTO instance with all fields populated as per actual schema. This operation is a standard detail retrieval complementary to user search and account management endpoints.
operations.summary: Retrieve the full details of a single registered Todo List user by userId.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target Todo List user.

responseBody.description: Detailed user information for the specified userId.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation updates a registered user's account information. It operates on the todo_list_users table, which is the primary entity for user management in the Todo List service. Users can update core profile data fields excluding sensitive authentication details via this endpoint. Updates must conform to business rules concerning data validation, uniqueness (particularly for email), and auditability (timestamps are updated accordingly). The system enforces a policy that certain fields (such as password hashes and deletion status) cannot be directly updated via this endpoint — only profile-maintainable fields are exposed. The operation supports full replacement of updatable user fields based on provided input, strictly adhering to validation requirements and unique constraints as described in the Prisma schema.
operations.description:
Update an existing user's profile in the Todo List application by providing new values for allowable fields. This endpoint supports the update of essential profile details—such as email or optional profile-oriented fields—but does not allow modification of authentication credentials, account status flags, or deletion timestamps.

All update requests must be authenticated—the actor must be an authorized system user or administrative actor. Business validation ensures uniqueness constraints (such as unique email) and mandatory fields are respected. Every update results in an updated audit timestamp, and any attempted updates to forbidden fields will result in a validation error.

This operation leverages the user entity from the todo_list_users table, ensuring that only permissible fields as defined by the business model can be altered through this endpoint. Integration with business rules ensures compliance with email formatting, locked status policies, and referential integrity throughout the update process.
operations.summary: Update an existing user profile in the todo_list_users table.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target user in the Todo List application. Required to specify which user account will be updated.

requestBody.description: Data object containing the new values for the user's updatable profile fields (such as email and profile-related metadata). Fields like password hash, deleted_at, or status cannot be updated via this API.

responseBody.description: Returns the updated user account record after applying the requested changes. Shows latest values for all profile fields (excluding sensitive authentication credentials).

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation performs the full, irreversible deletion of a user's account in the Todo List application. It is implemented on the todo_list_users table, ensuring that the user's entire profile and all related personal information are permanently removed from the system. The design strictly prohibits soft deletion, following the business rule that deletion must result in actual removal from the database, as dictated by the deleted_at field logic (hard delete policy). Deletion operations are audited, and all data tied to the user, including related todos, will be subject to cascading delete or full clean-up according to referential integrity rules.
operations.description:
Permanently erase a user's account from the Todo List service, ensuring no residual personal or account data remains in the database. This operation can only be performed by authorized system actors—typically the user themselves or an administrative actor, depending on business policy and privacy compliance requirements.

Upon execution, all associated personal data, including referenced todos, are also processed for removal according to the underlying foreign key/mapping strategies. This process is non-reversible and intended for final account removal situations such as user-requested account deletion, privacy regulation compliance, or administrative intervention for user removal.

The endpoint leverages the hard deletion policy of the todo_list_users table, ensuring that audit and referential clean-up steps are performed as part of the lifecycle, fully aligning with security and business practice expectations.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a user's account from the todo_list_users table.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target user to be deleted from the Todo List application. Required to indicate the specific user account for removal.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of session records associated with a specific user account. It is based on the todo_list_user_sessions table, which tracks authenticated login instances, session lifecycles, and audit metadata for all registered users. This endpoint is primarily intended for administrative oversight and security auditing—allowing authorized actors to review the login history, device metadata, activity location, and session expiration/active status for any user. The underlying session entity enforces traceability, strict linkage to todo_list_users via the foreign key, and supports comprehensive searching by user, creation date, expiration, or IP address.
operations.description:
Obtain a complete login and session activity history for a specific user by searching and filtering their todo_list_user_sessions records. This endpoint supports complex queries with pagination, sorting, creation date filtering, and IP-based lookup, giving detailed insight into the user's recent and historical authentication events.

Authorization is restricted by system configuration; due to constraints only the "user" actor is available, so this endpoint is set as public (no explicit actor). Session records include information such as session initiation time, expiration or revocation time, source IP, user agent/referrer, and associated user ID. This API is strictly read-only for analysis, and session creation or deletion is handled through the authentication subsystem, not this endpoint.

This operation reflects the subsidiary nature of the todo_list_user_sessions table, which does not support independent creation or manual deletion of sessions. Modifications and new sessions are managed exclusively through the authentication subsystem, so this API is strictly read-only.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of user sessions (todo_list_user_sessions) for a specific user account.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the user whose sessions are being queried.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for advanced session filtering, sorting, and retrieval for the selected user ID.

responseBody.description: Paginated result set of session summary records matching search criteria for the user.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the detailed session/login record for a specific session ID belonging to a given user. It operates on the todo_list_user_sessions table, providing fine-grained, field-level audit metadata about the session, such as authentication time, IP, referrer, device/endpoint, and session expiration. Access to this endpoint is governed by system role constraints; only actors defined in schema ("user") are valid, so this endpoint is set as public (no explicit actor). This is a read-only audit endpoint implementing robust traceability for user account security and compliance analysis. The API ensures that the session explicitly belongs to the provided user ID to guarantee account-bounded security separation.
operations.description: Fetch all field details for a single user session, including activity timestamp, IP, login context, and expiration or revocation status. This endpoint is designed for audit and forensic analysis, supporting full field-level data extraction for a single session instance. The API loads the session record, validates user-session linkage, and exposes all related audit fields according to the session schema. This is a read-only operation: session creation, modification, and deletion must be handled through the authentication system, not this endpoint.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information for a specific user session (todo_list_user_sessions) by sessionId for the specified userId.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the user who owns the session.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the session to retrieve details for.

responseBody.description: Full audit and field details for the requested session record associated with the user.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation allows searching, filtering, and paginating through all todo items available to the authenticated user. It queries the Todo Item table in the Prisma schema to return todo tasks according to search criteria such as keyword, status, due date, or priority. Advanced search, sorting, and result pagination are implemented to support efficient scalable queries for lists of todos without retrieving all records at once. The operation responds with a paginated summary of matching todo tasks for client display.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of personal todo items for the current user. The operation supports advanced search queries including keyword search of the task name or description, status filtering (completed or not), filtering by date and other relevant constraints supported by the database schema.

The request supports pagination with standard page and page size parameters, as well as sorting by task due date and/or creation order. Results include todo summary data for each item, optimized for list rendering. All filtering and query logic is enforced server-side, so only matching items are returned to the requesting user based on their session.

Security is enforced by limiting results to todos owned by the authenticated user, and rate limiting protects against abusive list queries. Only todos belonging to the requester are shown. Related endpoints are available for viewing details and modifying tasks.
operations.summary: Search and paginate the authenticated user's todo items with advanced filters.

requestBody.description: Query filters, pagination, and sorting options for listing the authenticated user's todos.

responseBody.description: Paginated summary list of todo items matching user query filters and pagination settings.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the details of a specific todo task belonging to the authenticated user. It operates on the Todo Item table and is accessed using the unique identifier of the desired todo. Returns the complete data for the todo, including all its fields, according to the associated Prisma schema. The operation ensures data is only exposed if the user owns the requested item.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a single todo item by its unique identifier. The operation provides the complete task information for the authenticated user, such as task name, description, status, due date, and timestamps, reflecting the exact entity as stored in the database.

This endpoint requires the user to specify the todoId path parameter, which uniquely identifies the user's own task. If the todo belonging to the user is not found, an error is returned. Security checks enforce that users can only view their own tasks, with access denied for unauthorized requests.

This operation is associated with the inspection of a single todo entity for user review or client detail display. It is commonly paired with search and modify endpoints for full task management functionality.
operations.summary: Retrieve details for one of the authenticated user's todos by ID.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item to retrieve for the current user.

responseBody.description: Detailed todo item object containing all fields for the specified task.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item for an authenticated user. It operates on the todo_list_todos table in the database, which stores individual tasks for personal productivity management. The request body must supply all necessary fields for the todo, including a non-empty, user-unique title and (optionally) a description. The operation enforces maximum character limits and associates the new task strictly with the currently authenticated user (ownership is strictly enforced at database and business logic levels). Creation and update timestamps are automatically set. This operation does not allow creation for another user or system-wide todos—ownership is always constrained to the requestor.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables an authenticated user to create a new todo item in their own task list. The primary use is to record actionable tasks and reminders that are unique to the owning user. Only the authenticated user may create tasks for themselves—no cross-user or shared creation is supported for data privacy and boundary enforcement.

The operation will validate that the title is provided, non-empty, and does not exceed 100 characters. Uniqueness of the title is enforced within the user's own todos, preventing accidental duplication but allowing other users to use the same title independently. Optional description text, if present, must also adhere to a 1000-character limit. The status is initially set as 'incomplete', and timestamps for creation and update are automatically generated server-side. The task becomes visible only to its creator.

If a creation attempt violates uniqueness or field length constraints, the API returns descriptive error messages. Successful creation returns the fully detailed todo item, including metadata such as timestamps and current status. This operation integrates tightly with the todo_list_todos schema as documented in the database.
operations.summary: Create a new todo item (todo_list_todos table).

requestBody.description: Payload for creating a new todo item. Must include a user-unique title and may contain an optional description.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo item, including user ownership and all metadata fields.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo item belonging to the currently authenticated user in the todo_list_todos table. It allows the owner to modify the title, description, or completion status of their own todo. The item is identified by its UUID in the path. Validation rules ensure field length, scope uniqueness for titles, and logical transitions for status updates (e.g., marking as complete updates 'completed_at'). Ownership is strictly enforced—no user can update another's tasks. Auditing is supported via update timestamps.
operations.description:
This API endpoint allows an authenticated user to update their own todo item. The primary goal is to let users edit details of their tasks such as the title, description, or completion state. Every update operation is strictly validated for user ownership, ensuring data privacy and security—only the owner can change their own records.

Title edits must remain non-empty, within 100-character limits, and unique for the current user. Description, if supplied, is subject to the same 1000-character limit as during creation. Status transitions are validated to ensure logical consistency: changing from 'incomplete' to 'complete' sets the completion timestamp; reverting the status clears it. The 'updated_at' timestamp is modified on every update to ensure full auditability.

Any attempt to update a todo owned by another user, violate length constraints, or duplicate a title within the user's set will generate clear failure responses. The updated todo item is returned in full, reflecting all modifications and current state. Integration is tightly bound to the todo_list_todos model and its business requirements.
operations.summary: Update an existing todo item (todo_list_todos table) by id.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the todo item to update, owned by the authenticated user.

requestBody.description: Payload for updating an existing todo item. Fields may include title, description, and/or status.

responseBody.description: The updated todo item, including all changes, metadata, and current state.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a specific todo item from the underlying 'todo_list_todos' table. It accepts a path parameter identifying the unique todo via its UUID primary key. The operation enforces strict per-user ownership, ensuring that only the authenticated owner can delete their own task. It irreversibly removes the record from the data store and does not perform any form of soft deletion or archival; upon execution, the record and its completion history are purged permanently from the system. The operation is scoped for user-facing, single-entity deletion—bulk or cross-user deletion is strictly disallowed by both schema and business rules.
operations.description:
Permanently remove an individual todo item owned by the authenticated user. This operation is intended for situations where a user wishes to eliminate a completed or obsolete task from their personal todo list, as managed in the 'todo_list_todos' table.

The endpoint accepts the todo identifier as a required path parameter. Prior to deletion, the backend confirms that the caller is both authenticated and the registered owner of the task, as mandated by the foreign key constraint to user accounts. All deletion requests targeting tasks not belonging to the user are automatically rejected, upholding strict partitioning and privacy.

Deletion is irreversible—unlike soft deletion, no recovery or restoration is possible after this operation. Security policies enforce that only the authenticated task owner may initiate deletion. Attempts to delete already-removed or non-existent todos will return an appropriate error. Related operations include create (POST /todos), update (PUT /todos/{todoId}), and query (GET/PATCH methods on todos).
operations.summary: Permanently delete a single todo item from the todo_list_todos table.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo item to delete (UUID).

operations.name: erase

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

email.description: User email address used for registration and login. Must be unique in the todo_list_users table and conform to email format standards as required by registration policy. This is the primary user identifier for authentication.

password.description: User password in plain text. Must satisfy minimum security requirements (minimum 8 characters, containing both letters and numbers as per business policy). Sent in plain text for registration; backend hashes and stores only a secure hash in the database.

Client IP address for session audit. May be IPv4 or IPv6. Optional; server may extract if not provided.
When the IP address is unknown or not provided, the field should be set to null.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (e.g., previous page) at the time of registration. Required for traceability and audit. Can be an empty string (direct access) but must be present; must be a valid or empty URI.

ITodoListUser.IJoin.description:
User registration request for the Todo List application.

This type provides data to create a new user in the todo_list_users table, enforcing unique email and secure password policies. Email must be unique and conform to a valid format; passwords are supplied in plain text and hashed by the backend. Also includes session context fields (ip, href, referrer) for audit logging: href and referrer are required, ip is optional, supporting full security traceability during registration flows.

On successful registration, a pending user is created with an email verification process. Registration is denied if the email is duplicate, invalid, or the password is non-compliant.

This schema directly maps to the todo_list_users Prisma model for user fields, and supports creation of a related session record for auditing.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authorized user. This is the id field from the todo_list_users table, assigned at user creation. Required for all authentication and authorization workflows.

email.description: User email address used as the unique login credential. Must conform to email standards and is always unique among users.

is_verified.description: Flag indicating if email has been confirmed through the verification process. Used to enable or restrict access to certain authenticated features.

locked.description: Indicates whether the account is currently locked (e.g., due to failed login attempts, security incidents, or administrative actions).

oneOf.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) when the user account was locked due to authentication failures or administrative actions. Null if not currently locked.

locked_at.description: Timestamp when account was locked, or null if never locked.

oneOf.description: One-time token used for confirming user email verification. Populated during registration or re-verification processes; null if not currently in verification or already verified.

email_verification_token.description: Current email verification token, or null if no active token.

oneOf.description: UTC datetime when the last verification email was sent. Updated for each (re)verification flow; null if never sent or already verified.

email_verification_sent_at.description: When verification email was last sent.

oneOf.description: Unique token used when the user initiates a password reset flow; null if none in progress. Required for safe password resets.

reset_password_token.description: Password reset token for ongoing reset operation, or null if not active.

oneOf.description: Datetime when the last password reset token was issued for this account. Used for expiration and audit support; null if never initiated.

reset_password_sent_at.description: When password reset was last triggered.

created_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) when the user account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) for last update to user profile or status.

oneOf.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) if the user account was deleted, for audit/history. Null if account is active.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when user was deleted, or null if active.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized user response structure after successful join, login, or token refresh for the Todo List application.

Includes the user's UUID and the authorization token bundle (access and refresh tokens). Returned by all authentication and session management endpoints. The token is used for subsequent API authentication as specified by the backend security policy.

This schema is implementation of the IAuthorized pattern required for authentication APIs.

email.description: User email address, used as the primary login credential. Must be unique and conform to email format standards. Required for registration and login.

password.description: User password provided in plaintext for authentication. The server securely hashes and verifies against the password_hash column. Never stored or returned in plaintext.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking and audit. May be IPv4 or IPv6 depending on network context.
Client IP address for session tracking and audit. May be IPv4 or IPv6 depending on network context.

ip.description: Client IP address for session auditing; extracted by backend if omitted. Optional for login, but helps correlate device/location (supports IPv4 or IPv6, or null for auto-detect).

href.description: Current browser/page URL at time of login. Used to track session context and provide full connection metadata for audit. Must be included by the client for accurate session history.

referrer.description: Referrer (previous page URL) at start of login. Used as context metadata for the new session. Must be included by the client for proper audit compliance.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login credentials for authenticating an existing user to todo_list_users.

This type accepts the user's email and password in plaintext for verification, as well as session context fields (ip, href, referrer). The email must be a valid unique address. The password is securely hashed on the server. Session metadata fields (href/referrer) are required for audit and compliance, while ip is optional (client or backend provided).

Used as request body for user login endpoint.

refresh_token.description: Valid JWT refresh token identifying the current user session. Used to authenticate and extend session lifetime during token rotation. Must correspond to an active, unexpired, and unrevoked session record in todo_list_user_sessions.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Data required to refresh a user's authentication token and session state.

Includes the refresh_token string for session-based authentication, matching an active and non-expired session record. Token is validated against the sessions table and user policy. Used as request body for token refresh endpoint.

email.description:
User email address, used as the primary login credential in the todo_list_users table. This must match the registered email for the account targeted for verification.

The email is validated for RFC 5322 compliance and must be unique across all users. Used to look up the user's verification context and ensure proper identity matching during email confirmation.

email_verification_token.description:
One-time token used to confirm user email verification. This token must exactly match the value stored in email_verification_token for the target user. Provided as part of the verification email sent after signup.

Verification tokens are purposely random, cryptographically secure, and short-lived to prevent brute-force attacks or social engineering. Null after successful verification.

ITodoListUser.IVerifyEmail.description:
Request body DTO for verifying a newly registered user's email address to activate their account.

This schema is used when a user submits their one-time verification token, typically received by email, to complete registration. It validates the provided email and token pair against the fields in todo_list_users (email, email_verification_token), and triggers account activation if valid. Both fields are required. Upon success, is_verified becomes true and the token is cleared.

success.description:
Indicates if the email verification operation was successful. True if user account is activated and is_verified is now true; false otherwise.

Used as a primary outcome signal so clients can branch for UX (success page or error prompt).

user_status.description:
Describes the user's account status after verification attempt (e.g. "active", "verification_failed", "already_verified", "token_expired").

Used to explain status and enable finer-grained front-end flows beyond binary success/failure.

ITodoListUser.IVerificationResult.description:
Response body DTO for the outcome of a user's email verification attempt.

Returned to the client after attempting to activate the account with an email and token. Contains success boolean and a user_status string. Supports detailed UI and workflow handling for multiple verification outcomes.

email.description: User email address to initiate password reset procedure. This must be a valid email and is used as the primary credential for the user in the Todo List system. This property is required to initiate any password reset flow. Multiple requests for non-existent or ineligible accounts yield identical generic responses for security.

ITodoListUser.IResetPasswordRequest.description:
Request schema to initiate a password reset flow for a registered user account. 

Contains the account email which triggers an out-of-band reset-password workflow, if eligibility checks (existence, status) are met. This structure is security-hardened to prevent user enumeration by never indicating whether the email exists in the system. 

If the account is verified, unlocked, and not deleted, a reset_password_token and reset_password_sent_at will be generated and linked to the user, and a notification sent. Otherwise, the response is generic and does not reveal eligibility.

success.description: Always true. Indicates that the reset password process has been started according to policy. The value is deliberately generic to avoid user information leakage.

ITodoListUser.IResetPasswordRequestResul.description:
Response schema for a password reset request operation on the todo_list_users table.

For privacy reasons, this structure always returns success, regardless of whether the provided email exists or the account is eligible for reset. This prevents attackers from inferring the existence or status of user accounts in the system. Used to provide a constant, generic reply to clients in compliance with security requirements.

ITodoListUser.IResetPassword.description:
Password reset request DTO for registered users in the Todo List application.

Used for submitting a password reset with a valid reset_password_token and a new password for the account recovery process. On valid token and compliant new password, resets the user's password and wipes the used token and associated metadata. Response to this DTO results in updating todo_list_users' password_hash and revoking all sessions.

The password field is required; the backend hashes and stores it according to security policy. The reset_password_token must be an exact match for the user's latest reset token, and must not be expired.

The request enforces password policy requirements (minimum 8 characters, must include both a letter and a number). No authentication is performed for this endpoint, and responses are generic to prevent information leakage.

reset_password_token.description: Password reset token issued to the user via email or reset flow. Must exactly match the token in the user's record. Required and must be valid and unexpired. Provided as-is in request body for verification.

password.description: New plain text password to set for the account. Required and must adhere to security policy: at least 8 characters, including at least 1 letter and 1 number. The backend hashes this value before storage in password_hash. Password is never returned in responses.

ITodoListUser.IResetPasswordResult.description:
Password reset result DTO for the Todo List application.

Represents the outcome of an attempted password reset operation. Indicates whether the reset was successful or failed (e.g., invalid/expired token) in a generic, non-leaking way. Designed so the API never reveals whether a password reset token or email is valid to prevent enumeration attacks.

Used for response to ITodoListUser.IResetPassword requests, regardless of success.

Provides an is_success flag for client-side handling, and always supplies a message (which should be generic in case of error).

is_success.description: Indicates whether the password reset operation completed successfully. True if password was set, old tokens revoked, and the account is now recoverable with the new password. False if there was an invalid/expired token or the reset failed. Should not reveal the nature of failure to prevent leaking information about account existence or token validity.

message.description: A human-readable, non-specific message describing the result of the password reset operation. Should not disclose token validity, account existence, or any security-sensitive details. Used for user notification in all cases.

email.description: User email address used for login and identity confirmation during unlock. Must exactly match the registered email for the account that is locked. Required for verification and business rule validation as specified for the unlock process.

unlock_token.description: Token or secret for unlocking the locked user account. Typically sent by email (via previous verification or password reset request), or generated by admin/manual process depending on unlock business logic. Used to authenticate and authorize account unlock.

ITodoListUser.IUnlock.description:
Unlock process request schema for a locked user account in the Todo List system.

This schema includes credential fields required to validate and process the unlock workflow. Unlock operations require the registered email and a valid unlock token or code, which may be generated through email verification, password reset flow, admin intervention or other secure method.

On success, the user's locked status is cleared and their account may be accessed again, subject to business rules defined for account recovery. All fields are strictly validated to match business and audit requirements. Email must match a unique registered account; unlock_token must be an active, valid unlock code.

success.description: Whether the unlock operation succeeded (account unlocked and available for login). True if account status changed from locked to unlocked; false if unlock failed or credentials were invalid.

message.description: Detailed outcome message explaining the result of the unlock operation. On success, provides confirmation. On failure, provides a reason (e.g., invalid token, already unlocked, expired, etc.).

can_login.description: Whether the user is now eligible to attempt login after the unlock operation. True when the account is fully unlocked and not subject to cooldown; false if more steps are required or lockout remains.

next_step.description: Instruction or step to continue account re-entry or recovery if the unlock was not successful or more action is needed. May indicate password reset flow, cooldown period, or contacting support. Null or omitted if no further action is required.

ITodoListUser.IUnlockResult.description:
Unlock operation result schema for Todo List user account recovery workflows.

This schema is returned after processing an unlock request, and indicates the outcome of the unlock process. The result captures whether the operation succeeded, provides a message for user feedback, and indicates if the user is now eligible to log in. The 'next_step' field may be used to guide the user through remaining recovery workflows if the account cannot be fully unlocked yet.

This schema covers security requirements for account recovery, audit, and user communication in compliance with business rules and user experience standards.

ITodoListUser.description:
Registered user entity for the Todo List application.

Represents an individual account uniquely identified by email in the Todo List system. Used for authentication, account management, and as the actor/owner for all user data. Contains identity, authentication lifecycle markers, user status fields, and all metadata for administrative operations, compliance, and auditability.

Includes all fields required for the full user lifecycle: registration, authentication, verification, password reset flows, lockout and unlock events, and deletion lifecycle. These fields support business logic around secure account management, operational support, and full audit history of identity changes and access states.

The schema enforces business rules such as unique email, strict separation of authentication credentials (password hash never exposed via API), comprehensive account status markers (verification, locked, deleted), and compliance with privacy requirements (fields like tokens and timestamps are null unless in recovery, verification, or administrative flow context).

Excludes sensitive authentication (password hashes) from API responses for security. Fields related to email verification, password reset, and account status are exposed for operational auditing and compliance only for administrative/support actors. Lifecycle timestamps and token fields are included as nullable values and described for their specific business flow usage.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the user. Serves as the system primary key and stable reference for all user operations. Generated upon registration and remains constant for the entire account lifecycle.

email.description: User email address used as the unique login credential. Must conform to RFC 5322 email standards and is always unique among users. Required for registration, login, password reset, and verification processes.

is_verified.description: Flag indicating if the user's email has been successfully verified. Set to true upon completion of email verification flow, enabling access to full application features.

locked.description: Indicates whether the account is currently locked due to repeated failed login attempts, security incidents, or administrative actions. A locked state prevents all login attempts until unlock flow (manual/admin or business logic) clears the status.

oneOf.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) when the user account was locked due to authentication failures or administrative actions. Null if not currently locked.

locked_at.description: Timestamp when account was locked, or null if never locked.

oneOf.description: One-time token used for confirming user email verification. Populated during registration or re-verification processes; null if not currently in verification or already verified.

email_verification_token.description: Current email verification token, or null if no active token.

oneOf.description: UTC datetime when the last verification email was sent. Updated for each (re)verification flow; null if never sent or already verified.

email_verification_sent_at.description: When verification email was last sent.

oneOf.description: Unique token used when the user initiates a password reset flow; null if none in progress. Required for safe password resets.

reset_password_token.description: Password reset token for ongoing reset operation, or null if not active.

oneOf.description: Datetime when the last password reset token was issued for this account. Used for expiration and audit support; null if never initiated.

reset_password_sent_at.description: When password reset was last triggered.

created_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) when the user account was created. Populated automatically on registration.

updated_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) when the user profile or status was last updated. Used to support audit and compliance reporting for administration.

oneOf.description: Timestamp if the user account is scheduled for or has completed deletion. Null if the account is currently active.

deleted_at.description: When user account was deleted/removed, or null if still active.

ITodoListUser.IRequest.description:
Request query schema for searching Todo List users with rich filtering, sorting, and pagination support.

This DTO enables system administrators and internal auditors to efficiently locate user accounts by a range of criteria, including email, account status (locked and/or verified), and registration dates. It underpins protected query endpoints for account management and compliance auditing.

Fields support robust business logic for pagination (page, limit), flexible sorting (sort_by, sort_order), and edge cases such as tight date ranges or highly restrictive filtering. The schema is intended for use in internal systems only—never exposed in public/anonymous API operations.

page.description: Page index for paginated results. The first page is always 1. Exceeding the available number of pages yields a zero-length result set.

limit.description: The number of user records to return per page. Limited to ensure efficient queries (default 20; maximum 100 for admin screens).

email.description:
Exact email address filter: returns only the user with this specific email (case-insensitive). 

Supports account validation and targeted user audits, but never supports partial or fuzzy matching for privacy.

is_verified.description: If provided, will filter users according to their email verification status. True = only verified users, False = only unverified users; omitted = any.

locked.description: If provided, restricts the result set to only users whose account lock status matches this value. True = locked users (temporarily disabled access), False = active/unlocked; omitted = any.

from_date.description: Query boundary: return only users who registered at or after this UTC ISO8601 datetime. Useful for compliance or forensic queries by date of account creation.

to_date.description: Query boundary: return users registered at or before this UTC ISO formatted datetime. Commonly used for admin reports or audit slices.

oneOf.description: Sort by registration/creation date ascending or descending (see sort_order).
Sort by email address order (lexical, case-insensitive).

sort_by.description: Choose which user property to sort on (created_at or email). Only columns explicitly supported are allowed to avoid index performance and security risks.

oneOf.description: Ascending (A-Z or oldest-first) sort.
Descending (Z-A or newest-first) sort.

sort_order.description: Sorting direction for the resulting records (ascending or descending).

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description:
User summary data object for the Todo List application.

This schema provides a distilled view of the user entity, returning only the most fundamental identification data necessary to reference a user in lists and task ownership checks. It is designed to minimize personal data exposure, strictly omitting any authentication or security-sensitive attributes.

Used for embedding user references within todo lists, system search results, and ownership metadata. Is suitable for display in administrative screens and audit logs where extra information would infringe on user privacy or is unnecessary for the use case.

Field selection is intentional: only email (as unique identifier and notification address) and database UUID (for relational linkages) are provided. Excludes status, verification, or security flags, supporting both atomic lookups and GDPR/data minimization requirements.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the user account in the todo_list_users table. System-generated as a UUID v4 value and never reused.

This value is referenced in all relational data, user-owned objects (such as todo items), and administrative links. Ensures global uniqueness and prevents collisions when synchronizing identities across multiple instances or exporting data. Always present in every user summary.

email.description:
User's registered email address, guaranteed unique within the system. 

This email is the primary credential for user authentication, notification delivery, and identity proofing. It is validated for proper email format and ensured unique by database constraints. Visible in administrative overviews and reference objects, but never exposed in contexts requiring higher privacy (such as public listings).

User email address. Must be unique and conform to RFC email standards.

This is a profile field updatable by the user, subject to unique constraints and validation rules.

Cannot be set to null. Value must follow business logic for update operations and will trigger updated_at auditing.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating a registered user's account profile in the Todo List application.

Allows modification of updatable profile fields only. Excludes authentication credentials (password, password hash), system/ownership fields (id, deleted_at), and business logic-forbidden fields (locked, locked_at, is_verified, etc.).

All updates are strictly audited and validated for uniqueness and correct value formats. Ownership fields, authentication credentials, account lifecycles, and status flags are immutable through this DTO. This schema enforces the separation of updateable user-facing data versus system-internal data.

created_at_gte.description: Earliest session creation time to include in the query. Used for filtering session history results by lower bound on creation date.

created_at_lte.description: Latest session creation time to include in the query. Used for filtering session history results by upper bound on creation date.

expired_only.description: Whether to include only expired sessions (true), only active sessions (false), or all (omit for all).

ip_contains.description: Optional filter for searching for sessions initiated from IP addresses containing this search string fragment.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Must be a positive integer (1-based).

limit.description: Maximum number of session summary entries returned per page. Used for pagination and must be within [1, 100].

oneOf.description: Session sorting order field. Must be one of the fixed allowed values for consistent query and pagination ordering.
Session sorting order field. Must be one of the fixed allowed values for consistent query and pagination ordering.

order_by.description: Session sorting order field. Must be one of the fixed allowed values for consistent query and pagination ordering.

oneOf.description: Sort order for results (ascending or descending by chosen order_by field).
Sort order for results (ascending or descending by chosen order_by field).

order_direction.description: Sort order for results (ascending or descending by chosen order_by field).

user_agent_contains.description: Filter for sessions by user agent substring match (for device OS/browser audits, if available).

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering DTO for advanced query of session history records associated with a user in the Todo List application.

Allows filtering by creation time range, session expiration status, IP address fragment, and flexible pagination with custom sorting order. This type is used in session query APIs for security audits and login history pages. All fields are optional to allow piecemeal or full-dataset queries as required. This DTO supports both basic and advanced administrators' review scenarios.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Session and login audit entity for Todo List service.

Represents a concrete instance of a user's authenticated session, providing complete audit and forensic details for login activity, IP tracking, referrer, and session lifecycle. Each session is irrevocably linked to a user via foreign key, with context fields for IP, login endpoint, and referrer required for compliance and detailed auditing. Sessions enforce robust separation for user security and analysis and are not independently creatable by API users—managed via login/logout flows only.

All fields are returned read-only and are essential for security reporting, anomaly detection, and user-forensic queries. Session deletion or modification is only permissible through proper authentication flows (logout, password reset, or account deletion).

id.description: Unique session record identifier. Primary key for the todo_list_user_sessions table.

todo_list_user_id.description: User account identifier to which this session belongs. References {@link todo_list_users.id}. Enforces strict per-user session isolation and partitioning for all audit and security. Never supplied or modifiable from user input.

ip.description: Client IP address from which the session or login was initiated. Used for audit, user alerting, and security monitoring. Must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 literal.

href.description: The full frontend URL, SPA route, or endpoint address seen by the client at login or session creation. Required for complete audit-trails and debugging.

referrer.description: URL referrer at the moment of session creation. May be an empty string for direct accesses or when not applicable. Always required for full context; never null.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp of session creation event. Used for audit, default ordering, and compliance record-keeping.

expired_at.description: Timestamp marking when the session was expired or revoked. Null if session is currently active. Used for logout, session expiry, and audit purposes.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Query request filter and pagination settings for listing the authenticated user's todo items.

Allows paginated and filtered retrieval using keyword search, completion status, date filtering, and standard paging controls. Business validation is enforced for all filters and limits. This DTO is submitted to the server as the request body for filtered todo list queries supporting user-centric search and list render flows.

Security is handled by backend—this DTO never accepts user_id or any actor-identifying information. Pagination is enforced server-side for performance and to prevent over-fetching. All results are always scoped to current authenticated user only.

All field values are optional unless specified by API. Invalid or out-of-range limits/values are handled gracefully with validation errors.

keyword.description: Optional user-provided search keyword for filtering todo titles or descriptions. If present, must be 1-100 characters.

oneOf.description: Completion status to filter todos: 'complete' for finished tasks, 'incomplete' for unfinished. If omitted, returns both.
Completion status to filter todos: 'complete' for finished tasks, 'incomplete' for unfinished. If omitted, returns both.

status.description: Completion status to filter todos: 'complete' for finished tasks, 'incomplete' for unfinished. If omitted, returns both.

created_from.description: Lower bound (inclusive) filter for todo creation date. Must be ISO 8601 date or datetime format. Optional.

created_to.description: Upper bound (inclusive) filter for todo creation date. Must be ISO 8601 date or datetime format. Optional.

page.description: 1-based page number for paginated results. Defaults to 1. Must be a positive integer.

limit.description: Maximum number of todos to return per page. Defaults to 20. Must be between 1 and 100.

oneOf.description: Sort order for results: newest first ('created_at:desc') or oldest first ('created_at:asc'). Defaults to newest first.
Sort order for results: newest first ('created_at:desc') or oldest first ('created_at:asc'). Defaults to newest first.

order.description: Sort order for results: newest first ('created_at:desc') or oldest first ('created_at:asc'). Defaults to newest first.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a todo item as used in list and search views—provides only high-value attributes for overview and optimized performance.

Omits heavy/full properties such as 'description' or 'updated_at', focusing on minimal yet sufficient data for users to identify and distinguish their tasks at-a-glance.

Always references the owner by unique identifier and email via ITodoListUser.ISummary to ensure audit trails and correct partitioning. Used in pagination, search result rows, and filtered overviews. Business logic will never supply fields outside those defined here—this is a strict subset, never a superset, of the full ITodoListTodo entity.

id.description:
Unique identifier (UUID v4) for this todo item, as set in the todo_list_todos Prisma DB table.

Required for distinguishing between rows in any list or search result and for all subsequent detail/view actions.

title.description:
Task title, unique within the user's todo set. Mandatory; up to 100 Unicode characters enforced by the backend DB.

The primary label for user-facing todo listings, optimized for usability in pagination and fast search operations.

oneOf.description: Todo is currently open and actionable.
Todo has been finished by the user.

status.description:
Business completion status of the todo item. Accepts only 'incomplete' or 'complete' (as enforced by backend logic).

Enables quick filtering in overview screens or mobile lists.

completed_at.description:
UTC datetime when the todo was completed. Will be null/unset for tasks not yet finished.

Used for motivating, segmenting, and archiving completed items from list screens.

created_at.description:
UTC timestamp when the todo was originally added to the system.

Allows for ordering by date and age in overview/result UIs.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Represents a single todo item uniquely owned by one authenticated user within the Todo List application.

Provides the canonical structure mapping to the todo_list_todos Prisma table for both database and API response use. Used for returning the complete details of a todo in read, update, and create operations. Captures every field required for auditing, validation, and business functionality.

Each todo is exclusively tied to an owner (todo_list_users) and includes a user summary reference. The model enforces strict ownership: no sharing or transfer is possible. Field validation occurs for title uniqueness and length, optional description constraints, strict status (incomplete/complete, only), and controlled handling of completion and audit timestamps.

All fields directly correspond to column definitions in the Prisma schema; the structure is never extended by virtual fields or implementation artifacts. Deviations from this structure indicate a contract error in the backend or database configuration.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for this todo item within the system, generated as a version-4 UUID. Never reused or reassigned.

Required for every read, update, or delete operation. Enforces item uniqueness and supports system-wide traceability of actions.

user.description:
Reference to the summary record of the user who owns this todo. This is a strict foreign key relationship to the todo_list_users table, enforcing single-user ownership.

Ownership is immutable; a todo cannot be reassigned or shared. The summary reference provides just enough identity for audit and context without exposing sensitive fields.

title.description:
Short, unique title of the todo. Required; must be unique within the user's set and limited to a maximum of 100 Unicode characters.

Acts as the primary visible identifier in listings and detail displays. The backend enforces both length and per-user uniqueness for consistency and user experience.

description.description:
Long-form description or extra details for the todo. Optional; if provided, must be 1000 characters or fewer. Null if there is no description.

Intended to allow users to provide extended notes or context for more complex tasks. Backend validation ensures both maximum length and correct null handling.

oneOf.description: Todo has not yet been completed and remains actionable.
Todo is finished and can be filtered from incomplete views.

status.description:
Current business completion status of the todo. Only 'incomplete' or 'complete' values accepted—enforced by the system.

Controls display, filtering, and audit mechanisms for user productivity.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp (in UTC ISO 8601) of when this todo was marked as complete. Null if the item is still open or incomplete.

Used to audit completion events and reset status if the todo is re-activated.

created_at.description:
UTC timestamp marking when this todo was created. Set once at insertion and never updated thereafter.

Used for audit, default sorting, and lifespan analysis of tasks.

updated_at.description:
UTC timestamp recording the most recent update to this todo (content or status change). Set automatically by the backend for every API modification.

Supports full auditing and traceability of all user modifications.

title.description: Title of the todo item. Required; must be unique per user and limited to 100 Unicode characters.

description.description: Optional free-text description (up to 1000 characters) providing additional context for the task. If present, cannot exceed length constraint.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Payload for creating a new todo item belonging to the authenticated user.

Must include a non-empty, at-most 100 character title, unique within this user's todo list. Description is optional but, if provided, cannot exceed 1000 characters. User ownership is enforced server-side, so ownership fields are not accepted in client requests. Created/updated timestamps and status are managed automatically on the backend.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Request payload for updating an existing todo item owned by the authenticated user.

Allows modification of title, description, and completion status. Fields are all optional; omitted properties remain unchanged. Field validation ensures title uniqueness (per user), length, and logical status transitions. Ownership is strictly enforced via authentication context, not in payload.

Updates the updated_at timestamp automatically; completion state changes set or clear completed_at accordingly.

title.description: New title of the todo item (if updating). Must remain unique per user and comply with length limits.

description.description: Updated description (if changing). Null to remove description.

oneOf.description: Completion status: set to 'complete' or 'incomplete'. Transitions are validated to update completed_at correctly.
Completion status: set to 'complete' or 'incomplete'. Transitions are validated to update completed_at correctly.

status.description: Completion status: set to 'complete' or 'incomplete'. Transitions are validated to update completed_at correctly.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a registered user's login/audit session.

Provides compact session context for security logs, activity monitors, and access tracking, referencing the owning user via .ISummary. Contains only non-sensitive audit/event data required to display a session in lists or summaries.

Excludes full session metadata and never includes JWT or refresh tokens.

id.description: Session identifier. Uniquely identifies a login record/audit event for the owning user session.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user session was created. Used for chronological sorting and audit display.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when session expired, revoked or was completed. Null if session is still active.
